localBiteReport: The most recent available reporting for Choctawhatchee Bay is from the week of September 4–10, 2026 (approximately one to two weeks old), so conditions may have shifted slightly since then. Capt. Blake Nelson of Last Cast Charters reported that baitfish schools — primarily greenies — have been pushing from open water into bayous, grass flats, bridge areas, and roll-downs throughout the bay, which is setting up improving redfish and general flats activity as September moves toward October. Nelson noted that redfish, black drum, and trout have been holding in slightly deeper water and around dock and bridge structure during the ongoing heat, with a 3-inch Gulp Shrimp on a quarter-ounce jig head serving as a reliable search bait around docks. A local Santa Rosa Beach guide also reported active speckled trout in the bay just six days ago, including at least one bull redfish over 40 inches landed by a client. Water temperature at this location today is 87°F, and early morning or evening trips remain the most productive windows for bay inshore species as the fall transition builds.
